blocking_issues: The dead-man's-switch graft is architecturally impossible as specified: 'a tiny launchd health-check that alerts the phone when the laptop goes unreachable' cannot run — when the laptop is asleep, powered off, or offline, nothing on the laptop can send the alert. As written, the one piece of custom glue code the grafts add would ship and silently never fire in exactly the scenarios it exists for (power cut, sleep misconfig, ISP outage).

The VS Code terminal profile `tmux new -A -s vscode-N` is a static command line — VS Code profiles cannot generate a unique N per terminal, so every integrated terminal attaches to the SAME tmux session as a mirrored client of one shell. Phase 3's deliverable ('every VS Code terminal captured, persistence for free') breaks the moment the user opens a second terminal, which is day one.

The reboot path is completely unhandled: launchd LaunchAgents (happy daemon, caffeinate, code tunnel) only start after user LOGIN, and FileVault (macOS default) blocks unattended boot entirely — any power blip, kernel panic, or auto-installed macOS update leaves the machine dead until someone is physically home. Also, `pmset -c sleep 0` + caffeinate do NOT prevent clamshell sleep: a MacBook with the lid closed and no external display sleeps anyway. The plan configures the sleep case but ships nothing for reboot/lid, despite naming laptop-down as the most likely real outage.

A load-bearing security claim is asserted, not established: 'nothing sensitive rides Expo/APNs' assumes Happy's push payloads are content-free/ID-only. The research only establishes that Happy pushes on permission requests and that Expo offers NO payload E2E (Expo staff can read payloads). If Happy embeds session names or prompt text in notifications, plaintext agent activity transits Expo and APNs — directly contradicting the E2E story the whole transport section rests on.

Phase 1's deliverable contains three false-or-missing prerequisites: (a) Dispatch requires the Claude Desktop app running on the laptop — not installed, not in scope; (b) Blink mosh requires mosh-server on the laptop (`brew install mosh` is absent — only tmux is listed) plus a running SSH server for bootstrap; (c) Tailscale SSH *server* on macOS requires the open-source tailscaled variant — the App Store GUI app cannot accept incoming Tailscale SSH, so 'enable Tailscale SSH' as written does nothing.

The unverified-assumption surface is wider than the three items the grafts pull forward, and several sit under Phase 2's core deliverable, not optional phases: (a) Happy working on subscription OAuth with `happy connect` never invoked is asserted, never verified — nothing confirms no credential or transcript-adjacent secret leaves the laptop; (b) Gemini support in Happy is literally listed as 'deprecated' in the research, yet Phase 2 promises Gemini via generic ACP — unestablished; (c) self-hosted push delivery could be structurally impossible (if Happy enabled Expo push-security access tokens, only Happy's maintainers' servers can send to store-app tokens), and the Phase-4-reorder graft commits to self-hosting before this is checked; (d) VibeTunnel attaching to PRE-EXISTING tmux sessions is not established — research only shows it proxies terminals launched through its `vt` wrapper, so Phase 3's 'view every tmux terminal' deliverable is unverified; (e) single-writer session discipline is adopted as habit, but a habit is not a mechanism — one absent-minded `claude --resume` while the daemon owns the session is the assumed transcript-corruption failure mode.
fixes: Invert the direction: the LaunchAgent sends a content-free ping to a free external dead-man monitor (e.g. healthchecks.io) every 5 minutes; the monitor's iOS app/email alerts the phone when pings STOP. ~1 hour of work, no custom infra, no payload content leaves the laptop. This is the correct implementation of the graft's intent and should stay in Phase 1.

Point the VS Code terminal profile at a ~5-line wrapper script: parse `tmux list-sessions`, pick the first unused `vscode-N`, exec `tmux new -A -s vscode-$n`. Crash-orphaned sessions stay listed for reattach, preserving the persistence benefit. While in .tmux.conf, make the graft's 'window-size policy' concrete: `set -g window-size largest` so a phone-attached client can never shrink laptop panes (control-mode clients already don't; regular Blink attaches do under the 'latest' default).

Configure the reboot story explicitly: `sudo pmset -a autorestart 1` (auto-reboot after power failure); turn OFF automatic macOS update installation and apply updates only when home; keep the lid open or set `sudo pmset -a disablesleep 1`. Then make the FileVault decision consciously: keep FileVault ON and accept 'unattended reboot = down until physically home' with the dead-man alert (fix 1) as detection — do NOT trade to FileVault-off + auto-login for a laptop whose whole feature is remote code execution. Document the accepted downtime mode.

Add a week-one spike: trigger a real approval, inspect the actual delivered push payload (long-press the notification; check what text renders on the lock screen; optionally proxy the daemon's outbound Expo POST). If payloads carry session/prompt content, disable content in Happy's notification settings if such a setting exists, or accelerate self-hosting with the notification sender patched to ID-only — and treat every push strictly as a fetch-trigger regardless of outcome.

Amend Phase 1 scope: install Claude Desktop (or delete Dispatch from the deliverable); `brew install mosh` and enable macOS Remote Login (system sshd, reachable only over the tailnet — it survives at the login window, unlike LaunchAgents, which also partially mitigates the reboot issue) as the mosh bootstrap. Drop 'Tailscale SSH' unless willing to run the open-source tailscaled variant instead of the GUI app; plain sshd-over-tailnet is the simpler, equally-private story and mosh needs sshd anyway.

Extend the grafts' spike list into one explicit week-one checklist with pass/fail actions: (a) after Happy pairing, audit ~/.happy and the daemon's outbound traffic to confirm no API key/OAuth token leaves the laptop and `happy connect` was never invoked — fail means stop and reassess before Phase 2 completes; (b) test Gemini via `--experimental-acp` under Happy — fail means Gemini is a tmux-mirrored terminal, note it and move on; (c) killed-state notification handling on the real iPhone (already grafted — keep); (d) run the self-hosted-push spike BEFORE committing the Phase-4 reorder — if Expo push security blocks third-party senders, stay on the hosted relay knowingly and the reorder collapses back to original phasing; (e) verify `vt tmux attach -t <name>` surfaces pre-existing sessions in VibeTunnel — fail means Phase 3 is Blink-only, which is acceptable; (f) mechanize single-writer: a shell alias/wrapper for `claude` that checks the happy daemon's session list before honoring `--resume` and warns/refuses if the daemon owns that ID, plus habitual use of Happy's built-in one-keypress handoff as the release mechanism.
overengineering_flags: Phase 3 VibeTunnel is a third phone app plus a menu-bar service duplicating what Blink+mosh+tmux already delivers, for a surface that is glance-and-nudge only (80-120 col panes with pan/zoom on a phone). The design correctly keeps all real agent interaction in Happy's message-level chat UI — which is exactly why the terminal surface can start minimal. Run a week on Blink alone; add VibeTunnel only if mosh UX actually grates.

A standing `code tunnel` LaunchAgent keeps a 24/7 Microsoft-relayed full-IDE endpoint alive for a break-glass feature. Keep the command documented and start it over SSH the day it's needed — a break-glass tool should not be a standing service (also a security-surface reduction).

Keeping the Phase 1 `claude remote-control` tmux session running permanently after Phase 2: it is directory-bound, silently killed by env vars, and fully redundant once Happy works. Document how to relaunch it in two minutes; do not maintain it as a standing parallel lane.

Phase 5 and the adopted losing-design terminal-adapter blueprints: correctly deferred — keep them as notes and invest zero until the two-app UX has demonstrably failed after weeks of real use. Forking a fast-moving Expo monorepo is the one place this plan can quietly become the greenfield build it set out to avoid.

Docker/OrbStack running 24/7 solely to host one Node service for one user (Phase 4) is acceptable since it's the upstream-supported path, but resist adding anything around it — no compose stacks, no reverse proxy beyond `tailscale serve`. If the image misbehaves, the simplification direction is happy-server directly under launchd, not more container infrastructure.
The top-level estimate_days of 1.5 is misleading — phases 1-4 sum to ~6.5 days even before the grafted spikes. Not a design flaw, but budget a week and a half of evenings, not a weekend.
security_findings: Hosted-relay window (Phases 2-3): an unaudited codebase with a documented key-custody failure (Discussion #680 — 'E2E' marketing while server-decryptable API keys) carries the agent-control channel, and its E2E claim is self-asserted. Metadata (IPs, timing, message sizes) is visible to the operator regardless. The reorder graft moving self-hosting to right after Phase 2 is the correct mitigation and should be endorsed — conditional on the self-hosted-push spike passing first.

Push payload plaintext exposure (blocking issue 4): until the payload spike confirms ID-only content, assume permission-request text may transit Expo and APNs readable — Expo explicitly offers no payload E2E.

A stolen unlocked phone is remote code execution on the laptop: the device holds Happy's pairing keys, the Tailscale identity, and the SSH client config simultaneously. Enable Happy's biometric app lock if it exists (verify); rehearse both revocation paths once — remove the device in the Tailscale admin console AND unpair/rotate keys in Happy — so revocation is muscle memory, not documentation.

The Tailscale SSO account is now the root of trust for laptop access: whoever controls that Google/GitHub/passkey identity can join a device to the tailnet and reach sshd/happy-server. Mandatory: passkey or hardware-key 2FA on the identity provider account backing Tailscale.

Bind-address audit required at each phase: VibeTunnel and any `code serve-web` must listen on localhost or the Tailscale interface only (never 0.0.0.0), connection tokens kept; `tailscale funnel` must never be enabled on the happy-server serve config — one wrong flag converts the zero-public-endpoint design into a public RCE endpoint.

Remote spawn is unbounded RCE by design once paired: any directory, any agent, no allowlist — the allowlisted-project-roots graft only materializes if the Phase 5 fork or an upstream config hook exists. Interim containment: exactly one paired device in Happy, periodic review of the daemon's session log in ~/.happy, and conscious acceptance of the residual risk.

The /remote-control fallback lane stores session transcripts on Anthropic servers un-E2E'd and dies silently under DISABLE_TELEMETRY/DO_NOT_TRACK/custom base URL. Acceptable as a fallback for a subscription user, but do not reflexively route sensitive-repo sessions through it once Happy is primary.
